recon_facts.C1_basis_vendor_verbatim: 'Restarts. The window is kept on our side, under the SHA-256 of the reference. A client that restarts with the same reference keeps its count.' (#3866 comment 7113377492)
recon_facts.C2_basis_vendor_verbatim: 'A fresh reference. It costs nothing, and its pending count starts at zero. What remains is the ledger: a settled payment counts once our reader has it, a median of about 2.7 hours after its block and under 10 hours for 99 in 100. Inside that delay a fresh reference sees neither the earlier check nor the payment.' (#3866 comment 7113377492)
recon_facts.C3_basis_vendor_verbatim: 'A skipped hook. It leaves no decision on our side. The settlement is on chain and enters the ledger, so an operator can list payments that have no signed receipt beside them. Nothing does that for the operator today.' (#3866 comment 7113377492)
recon_facts.datapoint_reason_format: vendor datapoint (#3866 comment 7095709394, 23 Nov 2026 08:37 UTC): same $200 again to the same payee -> block, reason 'new_payee_window_above_max:200+200>250/168h'; limits count checks, not settlements; the cap is per payee address with a limit of three new payees a day
recon_facts.pending_semantics: each decision object carries pending: what the Gate counted (decisions, usd) for the same client_ref in the last 12 hours and has not yet seen on chain (gate.context.v2); without client_ref: {counted: false}
recon_facts.no_retry_rule: every check is written exactly once at the moment it is made; a failure, timeout or throw is a result and is recorded verbatim — never retried

scenarios.case: restart persistence: ref R1, payee P1, $200 -> allow; node process restart (new pid; client-side hook is stateless; nothing on the vendor side is touched or deleted); same R1/P1 $200 again
scenarios.expected: allow -> block; the block reason matches the vendor datapoint format new_payee_window_above_max:200+200>250/168h; store not deleted (outside the freeze)

scenarios.case: fresh-reference farming: payee P1, ten consecutive $200 checks, new reference each (FR01..FR10)
scenarios.expected: all 10 allow; every fresh reference's pending starts clean — no cross-reference aggregation (each pending.usd reflects at most its own check, not the cumulative $2000); all 10 responses and pending counters recorded

scenarios.case: amount splitting: one $300 intent split into five $60 checks across five references (SR1..SR5), payee P2
scenarios.expected: all 5 allow; the window math never sees $300

scenarios.case: payTo rotation: four distinct payee addresses P3, P4, P5, P6, first check each, one fixed reference RR1, $200 each
scenarios.expected: 1st-3rd allow (3 new payees/day); 4th -> blocked by the new-payee cap (the cap counts distinct addresses, not checks); the block reason recorded verbatim; a block by the $250 window instead of the cap is recorded as a divergence

scenarios.case: boundary arithmetic: ref R5, payee P6: $200 -> $50 (exactly 250 in window) -> $50
scenarios.expected: allow; allow (exactly 250 frozen under a strict > rule); block — if the boundary turns out inclusive, that is a finding

scenarios.case: race: 8 parallel identical checks, same reference RC1, same payload (P1, $200, exact/USDC/Base); response order recorded
scenarios.expected: frozen expectation is pending integrity: no double-count and no under-count — max pending.decisions across the 8 responses equals the number of allow decisions and max pending.usd equals 200 x that number; the decisions themselves and their order go in the report whatever they are

scenarios.case: skipped hook: a payment-creation attempt executed with no onBeforePaymentCreation hook registered
scenarios.expected: no externally observable signal (zero gate_check requests fired); the absence recorded as the result; a negative result is still a result

Control rows are the vendor's own disclosures (C1 restart survival, C2 fresh reference clean count, C3 skipped hook no signal) reproduced as controls, marked role: control; they are not findings — a control that fails its disclosure is recorded honestly.
Sessions 2, 3 and 7 are the ones the vendor's disclosure does not cover; if they come back clean, that is a positive statement about the hook and gets sealed the same way as a finding.

Pass rule for the final record: seal if all 7 sessions MATCH their frozen expected column; findings-type record if any session diverges — in both cases the record is complete: what matched, what did not. The offline table has zero empty cells: an unobservable field is recorded 'absent (by design)', never blank.
